sections.h2: What sort of county is Surry County?
sections.html:
Surry describes itself as foothills country in the Piedmont Triad region, with a large farm economy and a mixed industrial base. It lies in the Yadkin Valley Appellation, and its visitor draw includes Mayberry attractions and outdoor recreation.

The county dates to 1771, cut from Rowan, and once covered land now in Stokes, Forsyth and Yadkin. Dobson is the seat, and the tax and records offices are both there.

sections.h2: Where is the Surry County tax office?
sections.html:
At the Surry County Service Center, 915 East Atkins Street, Dobson, NC 27017, phone (336) 401-8100. It opens weekdays 8:15 to 5:00.

sections.h2: How does Surry County appraise about 44,000 parcels?
sections.html:
Appraisers sort the parcels into roughly 370 neighborhoods of similar homes, price land and buildings from sales, check the results in the field and office, then mail notices of value. The commissioners must approve the Schedule of Values, the manual of rates and adjustments, before it applies.

The county defines value as the most probable price in a competitive, open market and says periodic revaluation keeps some owners from paying more than their share while others pay less.

sections.h2: When did the last Surry County revaluation take effect?
sections.html:
January 1, 2025. In 2017 the commissioners moved the county from the eight year state maximum to a five year cycle, producing an effective date of January 1, 2021, and the county now calls itself a four year county.

Notices for 2025 were mailed in February 2025. Values hold until the next revaluation except for changes to a property. Ask the tax office when the next one takes effect.

sections.h2: Where do I take a Surry County value dispute?
sections.html:
Ask the Tax Department for an informal review, or file with the county's special review board. Surry appointed that board in 1982, the commissioners reappoint it each January, and it sits by the first Monday in May.

  • The board can change any value it finds out of line.
  • Each timely appellant may appear.
  • A losing appellant can go on to the state Property Tax Commission.

Bring documents showing why the value differs from market value, or facts about the property that affect it.

sections.h2: When does Surry County tax go delinquent?
sections.html:
Interest is added on payments made on or after January 6 following the due date: 2% the first month, then 0.75% for each month. The county calls the tax and interest charges non-negotiable.

It warns of garnishment, bank attachment, seizure of personal property and foreclosure under G.S. 105-365 to 105-368, and notes that remedies on real property must begin within 10 years of the due date. A delinquent real property list is posted on its collections page.

sections.h2: What does the circuit breaker do for a Surry County homeowner?
sections.html:
It caps tax at 4.0% of income up to the eligibility limit and 5.0% above it, up to 150% of the limit. NCDOR prints $38,800 and $58,200 for 2026, and an application is needed every year.

The owner must be 65 or disabled and must have lived in and owned the home for five years. Deferred tax becomes a lien, and three prior years come due when the owner sells, dies or moves out. The other two homestead programs, the elderly or disabled exclusion and the $45,000 disabled veteran exclusion, are filed on AV-9 with the county assessor, and an owner may use only one.

sections.h2: What should a Surry County seller do about taxes?
sections.html:
Ask Collections for a payoff before accepting an offer, because the lien on the parcel dates to the listing date and rides along until paid.

If the bill is behind, the tax pages carry a foreclosure section and the county can bring an auction action, with commissioner fees up to 5% of the price. Redemption before confirmation requires all taxes, penalties, interest and costs. Paying at closing is the usual fix.

faqs.q: Where is the Surry County Tax Department?
faqs.a: 915 East Atkins Street, Dobson, NC 27017, open weekdays 8:15 to 5:00.

faqs.q: When does interest start on Surry County property tax?
faqs.a: On payments made on or after January 6, at 2% for the first month and 0.75% each month after.

faqs.q: When did Surry County's current revaluation take effect?
When does Surry County's value review board meet?
faqs.a: It convenes each year by the first Monday in May.

faqs.q: Can I pay Surry County property tax in person?
faqs.a: Yes, at the drive-thru window at 915 East Atkins Street, or through the online portal.
